messages:
jordan: quick QA/design sync — debating how the playground run cards surface tool-call structured outputs. two ideas: (A) expand inline with smooth collapse/expand, (B) open a side panel for rich interactions. leaning inline for speed but worried about context loss.
priya: inline feels faster for quick scans. if we do inline, let's add a compact summary row (one-line) and a chevron to expand to full structured output. summary should show tool name + first field key/value. keeps list scannable.
matt: side panel is better for multi-step tools (with actions, copy buttons, logs). could we hybrid: inline summary + 'Open details' action that launches a panel for heavy interactions? that way default is lightweight.
jordan: yes hybrid. summary defaults inline, 'Open details' opens panel. microcopy note: use 'Open details' not 'View' or 'Inspect' — clearer for screen readers.
olga: a11y notes: (1) the expand button needs aria-expanded toggling and aria-controls -> id of the expanded region. (2) when panel opens, set focus to the panel heading and add aria-live="polite" to announce open state for screen reader users. (3) Make sure the inline summary isn't the only focusable element for the run card; there should be a clear keyboard affordance to expand.
priya: discovery: many users don't realize run cards are interactive. propose a subtle affordance: when the run list first mounts, animate the top run card with a 1-time nudge (fade + slight lift) and show a small label 'Press Enter to open' which disappears after interaction. non-intrusive and accessible.
matt: for keyboard mapping let's propose a tiny keymap in case eng needs it:
```
Enter -> expand focused run card (toggle)
O -> Open details panel for focused run
/ -> focus run search
Ctrl+ArrowLeft/Right -> switch between run tabs (All/Errors/Tool-calls)
Esc -> close panel or collapse inline output
```
oj: (typo) actually 'olga' not 'oj' :slightly_smiling_face:
jordan: also consider reduced-motion preference: the nudge animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion and fall back to a small border flash.
olga: color contrast: the 'Press Enter to open' pill uses low-contrast gray on gray in our mock; needs 4.5:1. Suggest using our accent token with 4.5:1 or adding a thin outline.
a11y-bot: quick report: https://ci.internal/a11y/reports/playground/run-cards-1722004321 (warnings: missing aria-controls ids, motion reduction not implemented on animation, 'Press Enter to open' contrast low).
priya: design followups: attach token suggestions and an outlined pill variant. also draft localized copy: in some languages 'Open details' becomes long; consider truncation rules + accessible tooltip.
matt: eng concerns: if we render lots of inline structured outputs, long pages will be heavy. suggest virtualized list + only render expanded outputs in DOM. also prefer lazy-loading panels for heavy content (logs, images).
jordan: agreed. action items: (1) design: provide pill styles + reduced-motion mock; (2) eng: virtualize list + lazy render expanded regions, implement keymap; (3) content: finalize microcopy + localization guidance; (4) a11y: add aria-controls, aria-expanded, focus management, announce open state. I'll create a short spec doc and drop a PR template.
olga: can someone add an e2e that simulates keyboard-only: focus list -> expand -> open details panel -> Esc back? catches regressions.
priya: I'll throw together a quick Figma frame and upload. linking here when ready.
jordan: thanks all — this feels like a good compromise. keep the inline summary very narrow (no more than 1 line preview) so run list density stays high.
